# logslice

Slice large, time-sorted log files by time range without reading them end to end.

`logslice` installs the `lslice` command, which prints only the lines between two timestamps.

## Highlights

- **Fast on big plain files:** `lslice` binary-searches byte offsets, so it reads a few blocks before the first match, whatever the file size.
- **Reads what you have:** plain `.log`, `.gz`, `.zst`, and standard input, in `nginx`, `iso`, `jsonl`, and `syslog` formats, auto-detected by default.
- **Human-friendly bounds:** use ISO 8601 (`2024-05-01T10:00`) or relative times (`-15m`, `-2h`, `-1d`).
- **Keeps stack traces whole:** lines without a timestamp stay with the nearest timestamped line above them.
- **No runtime dependencies:** `.zst` support is an optional extra.

## Quick start

You need Python 3.10 or newer. Clone the repository, then install it from the project root:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/example-org/logslice.git
cd logslice
pip install .
```

Print the requests between 10:00 and 10:05 from the bundled sample:

```sh
lslice --from 2024-05-01T10:00 --to 2024-05-01T10:05 examples/nginx-access.log
```

```text
198.51.100.7 - - [01/May/2024:10:00:03 +0000] "POST /api/orders HTTP/1.1" 201 87 "-" "curl/8.5.0"
203.0.113.24 - - [01/May/2024:10:01:15 +0000] "GET /api/orders/981 HTTP/1.1" 200 811 "-" "Mozilla/5.0"
203.0.113.10 - - [01/May/2024:10:02:12 +0000] "GET /health HTTP/1.1" 200 2 "-" "kube-probe/1.29"
198.51.100.7 - - [01/May/2024:10:04:59 +0000] "DELETE /api/orders/981 HTTP/1.1" 500 64 "-" "curl/8.5.0"
```

Check the install with `lslice --version`. You can also run `python -m logslice` instead of `lslice`.

## Usage

```text
lslice [--from TIME] [--to TIME] [--format FORMAT] [--tz ZONE] [--count] [FILE ...]
```

Common tasks:

```sh
# The last 15 minutes of a live log
lslice --from -15m /var/log/nginx/access.log

# Count matching lines in a compressed archive
lslice --count --from 2024-05-01T10:00 --to 2024-05-01T11:00 access.log.gz

# Slice a stream
journalctl -o short-iso | lslice --from -1h
```

| Option | Default | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--from TIME` | start of input | Inclusive start. |
| `--to TIME` | end of input | Exclusive end. Must be later than `--from`. |
| `--format` | `auto` | One of `auto`, `iso`, `nginx`, `jsonl`, `syslog`. |
| `--tz` | `$LOGSLICE_TZ`, else `UTC` | IANA time zone for timestamps without an offset. |
| `--count` | off | Print only the number of matching lines. |
| `FILE` | standard input | One or more files; `-` reads standard input. |

Format details:

- `jsonl` reads the timestamp from the key `ts`, `time`, or `timestamp`.
- `syslog` timestamps have no year, so `lslice` assumes the current year.
- `auto` detects the format from the first line it reads.

### Input requirements

- Input must be sorted by time. Both the binary search and the early stop at `--to` rely on it.
- Only plain files are searched by offset. `.gz`, `.zst`, and standard input are scanned from the start.
- To read `.zst` files, install the extra: `pip install 'logslice[zstd]'`.

### Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | At least one line matched. |
| `1` | No lines matched. |
| `2` | Bad arguments, an unreadable file, or `.zst` input without the `zstd` extra. |

## Development

```sh
pip install -e ".[dev,zstd]"
make test   # python -m pytest -q
make lint   # ruff check src tests
```

CI runs lint and tests on Ubuntu and macOS with Python 3.10, 3.11, and 3.12. See the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md) for release history.

A small `fetch` wrapper for Node.js 18 and later: retries with backoff, per-attempt timeouts, and typed JSON.

```bash
npm install @example-org/fetchkit
```

```ts
import { createClient } from "@example-org/fetchkit";
```

# grepl

A minimal grep-like filter written in Go. It reads lines from standard input and prints those that match a regular expression.

## Installation

Requires Go 1.22 or later.

```sh
go install github.com/example-org/grepl@latest
```

Or build from source:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/example-org/grepl.git
cd grepl
go build -o grepl .
```

## Usage

```
grepl [-i] [-v] PATTERN < input
```

`grepl` only reads from standard input; it does not take file arguments. Exactly one `PATTERN` is required.

| Flag | Description                      |
| ---- | -------------------------------- |
| `-i` | Case-insensitive match           |
| `-v` | Print lines that do **not** match |

Flags must come before the pattern.

### Examples

```sh
# Lines containing "error"
cat app.log | grepl error

# Case-insensitive
cat app.log | grepl -i warning

# Lines that do not contain "debug"
cat app.log | grepl -v debug

# Regular expressions
ps aux | grepl '^root\s+\d+'
```

## Regular expression syntax

Patterns use Go's [`regexp`](https://pkg.go.dev/regexp) package (RE2 syntax, see the [syntax reference](https://pkg.go.dev/regexp/syntax)). This is similar to `grep -E`, but without backreferences or lookaround.

## Exit status

| Code | Meaning                                                      |
| ---- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `0`  | At least one line was printed                                |
| `1`  | No lines were printed                                        |
| `2`  | Usage error or invalid pattern (message written to stderr)   |

## Limitations

- Input lines longer than 64 KiB are not supported (the default `bufio.Scanner` limit); reading stops at such a line without an error message.
- Standard input only; no file or directory arguments.
- No `-n`, `-c`, or other grep options.

# lisa-skills **Reusable AI agent skills for everyday workflows.**
Built for personal use, shared with the community. [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-2ea44f?style=flat-square)](LICENSE) [![Format: Agent Skills](https://img.shields.io/badge/format-Agent%20Skills-6e40c9?style=flat-square)](https://agentskills.io) [![Install with npx skills](https://img.shields.io/badge/install-npx%20skills%20add-cb3837?style=flat-square&logo=npm&logoColor=white)](#quick-start) [![Last commit](https://img.shields.io/github/last-commit/LisaHQ/lisa-skills?style=flat-square&color=0969da)](https://github.com/LisaHQ/lisa-skills/commits/main) [Quick start](#quick-start) · [Skill catalog](#skill-catalog) · [Usage](#usage) · [Create a skill](#create-a-skill) · [Contributing](#contributing)
**lisa-skills** is a curated collection of skills that teach AI agents to handle everyday tasks consistently. Each skill is a small folder of readable Markdown instructions: install it once, and your agent applies it whenever a task calls for it — no copy-pasting prompts. Skills follow the open [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) format, supported by Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, and many other agents. ## Highlights - 🎯 **Focused** — Each skill does one job, with clear inputs, outputs, and success criteria. - 🔍 **Grounded** — Skills work from evidence in your project, not assumptions. - 🧩 **Portable** — No hard-coded names, brands, or paths; skills adapt to any project. - 🪶 **Lightweight** — Plain Markdown you can review before installing, loaded only when a task needs it. ## Skill catalog | Skill | What it does | | --- | --- | | 📝 [**commit-message**](skills/commit-message/SKILL.md) | Writes accurate, concise commit messages from your actual Git or SVN changes. | > [!TIP] > Run `npx skills add LisaHQ/lisa-skills --list` to see the current catalog > from your terminal without installing anything. ## Quick start You need [Node.js](https://nodejs.org) (current LTS recommended) to run the [`skills`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills) CLI through `npx`. No Node.js? See [Manual installation](#manual-installation). **1. Install the skills** ```bash npx skills add LisaHQ/lisa-skills ``` The CLI detects the agents on your machine and guides you through the remaining choices. **2. Ask your agent** Start a new session and describe the task in plain language — for example, *"Write a commit message for my changes."* Your agent loads the matching skill automatically. **3. Stay up to date** ```bash npx skills update ``` ### Common commands | Task | Command | | --- | --- | | Preview skills without installing | `npx skills add LisaHQ/lisa-skills --list` | | Install a specific skill | `npx skills add LisaHQ/lisa-skills --skill commit-message` | | Install for all your projects | `npx skills add LisaHQ/lisa-skills --global` | | Install for specific agents | `npx skills add LisaHQ/lisa-skills --agent claude-code codex` | | List installed skills | `npx skills list` | | Update installed skills | `npx skills update` | | Remove a skill | `npx skills remove commit-message` | > [!NOTE] > By default, skills install into the current project (for example, > `.claude/skills/` for Claude Code), so you can commit them and share them > with your team. Add `--global` to install them in your user directory (for > example, `~/.claude/skills/`) and use them in every project. ### Manual installation Every skill is just a folder, so you can also copy it into your agent's skills directory by hand. For Claude Code: ```bash git clone https://github.com/LisaHQ/lisa-skills.git mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills cp -r lisa-skills/skills/commit-message ~/.claude/skills/ ``` To limit a skill to one project, copy it into that project's `.claude/skills/` folder instead. Other agents read skills from their own folders — see your agent's documentation or the [skills CLI's list of supported agents](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills#supported-agents). ## Usage Skills work in the background: there are no commands to memorize. - **Just ask.** Describe what you need. Your agent compares the request with each skill's description and loads the right one. - **Call a skill by name.** Many agents also let you invoke a skill directly — in Claude Code, type `/` (e.g., `/commit-message`). - **Fine-tune with options.** Add details in plain language, such as *"only my staged changes"*, or pass arguments like `/commit-message scope=staged`. For example, with the `commit-message` skill: > **You:** Write a commit message for my staged changes. > > **Agent:** Scope: staged (HEAD → index) — 3 files selected. > > ```text > Support per-job retry limits > > Commit description: > - feat(retries): Allow each job to override its retry limit; zero disables retries. > ``` The skill only drafts the message. It never stages, commits, or pushes without your permission. ## How skills work A skill is a folder containing a `SKILL.md` file: a short YAML header with a `name` and `description`, followed by step-by-step instructions for the agent. 1. **Discover** — At startup, the agent reads only each skill's name and description. 2. **Activate** — When a request matches a description, the agent loads that skill's full instructions. 3. **Execute** — The agent follows the workflow, opening bundled references or scripts only when needed. Because full instructions load on demand, you can keep many skills installed with very little overhead. Learn more at [agentskills.io](https://agentskills.io). ## Repository structure ```text lisa-skills/ ├── skills/ │ └── / │ ├── SKILL.md # Required: metadata and instructions │ ├── references/ # Optional: detailed docs, loaded on demand │ ├── scripts/ # Optional: helper scripts │ └── assets/ # Optional: templates and other resources ├── AGENTS.md # Conventions for AI agents working on this repo ├── CLAUDE.md # Claude Code–specific additions ├── LICENSE └── README.md ``` ## Create a skill 1. Scaffold a new skill from the `skills/` folder: ```bash cd skills npx skills init my-skill ``` 2. Edit `skills/my-skill/SKILL.md`: - **`name`** — Match the folder name, using lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens only. - **`description`** — Say what the skill does *and when to use it*. Agents rely on this text to decide when to load the skill. - **Instructions** — Keep the skill to one purpose, with clear inputs, outputs, and success criteria. 3. From the repository root, confirm that the skill is discovered: ```bash npx skills add . --list ``` 4. Test it with realistic requests, including incomplete, out-of-scope, and failure cases — not just the happy path. 5. Add the skill to the [skill catalog](#skill-catalog) with a one-line description. See [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) for the complete authoring and verification conventions, and the [Agent Skills specification](https://agentskills.io/specification) for the full format. ## Contributing Ideas, bug reports, and improvements are welcome. - **Report a problem or suggest a skill** — [Open an issue](https://github.com/LisaHQ/lisa-skills/issues). - **Propose a change** — Fork the repository, follow [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md), and open a pull request that explains what changed and how you tested it. Please keep personal data, credentials, and confidential material out of skills, examples, and logs. ## License Released under the [MIT License](LICENSE). Copyright © 2026 LisaHQ. ---

# CNC Operator Onboarding: VMC-3, Cell B

This folder is your training pack for running the VMC-3 vertical machining
centers in Cell B. Work through it in numbered order over your first three days.

## The rule that matters most

You may **not** run a machine unsupervised until both of these are true:

1. You passed the safety quiz with **at least 80%** (8 of 10).
2. Your trainer has **signed your training card**.

Until then, a trainer stays beside you whenever a machine is powered.

## Your first three days

| Day | Do this | File |
|-----|---------|------|
| 1 | Read the safety basics | `01-safety-basics.pdf` |
| 1 | Learn lockout/tagout (LOTO) | `03-lockout-tagout.md` |
| 2 | Machine overview slides | `02-machine-overview.pptx` |
| 2 | Learn the daily start-up checklist | `04-daily-startup-checklist.xlsx` |
| 3 | Run your first part with a trainer | `05-first-part/` |
| Any time after Day 1 | Take the safety quiz | `quiz/quiz-safety.md` |

Start with `00-welcome.md` for the short version of this plan.

## What's in each item

- **`00-welcome.md`**: overview and the sign-off rule.
- **`01-safety-basics.pdf`**: PPE, emergency stops and general cell safety (revision C).
- **`02-machine-overview.pptx`**: slides introducing the VMC-3.
- **`03-lockout-tagout.md`**: the 8-step procedure for isolating a machine before you reach inside it for maintenance, tool-change jams or coolant work. Learn it before you touch anything else.
- **`04-daily-startup-checklist.xlsx`**: the checklist you complete at the start of each shift (revision C).
- **`05-first-part/`**: the Day 3 exercise, Bracket A.
  - `instructions.md`: the steps.
  - `drawing-bracket-A.pdf`: the part drawing.
  - `O1001.nc`: the training G-code program (10 mm end mill, then 6.6 mm drill; metric).

- **`CHANGELOG.txt`**: version history of this pack.

## First-part reminders (Day 3)

Details are in `05-first-part/instructions.md`. In short: check the tool list
against the program header, set G54 on the vise's fixed jaw corner, and run the
first part in **single-block mode with rapid override at 25%**.

## Getting help

Ask the training coordinator (extension **214**) or your shift lead. If you are
unsure whether something is safe, stop and ask first.

# CNC operator onboarding: VMC cell

This three-day training pack prepares new operators to run the VMC-3
vertical machining centers in Cell B.

- **Day 1:** safety basics and lockout/tagout. **Day 2:** machine overview and
  the daily start-up checklist. **Day 3:** your first part, with a trainer
  beside you.
- You may run a machine without supervision only after you pass the safety
  quiz (8 of 10 correct) **and** your trainer signs your training card.
- Never reach inside the machine for maintenance, tool-change jams, or coolant
  work until you have completed [lockout/tagout](03-lockout-tagout.md).

## Start here

1. Read [00-welcome.md](00-welcome.md).
2. Work through the files in number order, following the day plan below.
3. If anything is unclear, ask the training coordinator (phone extension 214)
   or your shift lead.

## What's in the pack

| Day | File | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | [`00-welcome.md`](00-welcome.md) | The training plan and the rules for working without supervision |
| 1 | [`01-safety-basics.pdf`](01-safety-basics.pdf) | Required PPE in Cell B, emergency stops, and chip removal (rev C) |
| 1 | [`03-lockout-tagout.md`](03-lockout-tagout.md) | The eight lockout/tagout (LOTO) steps for the VMC-3 |
| 1 | [`quiz/quiz-safety.md`](quiz/quiz-safety.md) | The 10-question safety quiz; pass mark 80% |
| 2 | [`02-machine-overview.pptx`](02-machine-overview.pptx) | Machine overview slides (PowerPoint) |
| 2 | [`04-daily-startup-checklist.xlsx`](04-daily-startup-checklist.xlsx) | Daily start-up checklist (Excel, rev C) |
| 3 | [`05-first-part/instructions.md`](05-first-part/instructions.md) | Step-by-step exercise for your first part, Bracket A |
| 3 | [`05-first-part/drawing-bracket-A.pdf`](05-first-part/drawing-bracket-A.pdf) | Drawing BA-001 rev B: 6061-T6 aluminum, 100 x 60 x 12 mm stock |
| 3 | [`05-first-part/O1001.nc`](05-first-part/O1001.nc) | CNC program for Bracket A; the setup and tool list are in its header |

`quiz/answers.md` is the answer key. It is for trainers only, so don't open
it before you take the quiz.

## Safety essentials

These come from [01-safety-basics.pdf](01-safety-basics.pdf). Read the full
sheet on Day 1.

- Wear safety glasses with side shields at all times in Cell B.
- Wear hearing protection whenever the enclosure door is open.
- Wear safety shoes. Wear no gloves near a rotating spindle: a glove can catch
  and pull your hand in.
- Tie back long hair; no loose sleeves or jewelry.
- Emergency stops are the red mushroom buttons on the pendant and beside the
  door.
- Clear chips with a brush or chip hook, never by hand.

## Your first part (Day 3)

You run Bracket A with your trainer, in single-block mode with rapid override
at 25%. Follow [05-first-part/instructions.md](05-first-part/instructions.md)
step by step, and record your measurements on the inspection sheet together
with your trainer.

## Versions

The pack is at v2 (2024-08-12). See [CHANGELOG.txt](CHANGELOG.txt) for what
changed.

[![License: Apache-2.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache--2.0-blue)](LICENSE)
[![Python 3.10+](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.10%2B-blue)](pyproject.toml)

Turn titles in any language into clean URL slugs. Vietnamese tone marks and
`đ` are handled, so `Đường phố Hà Nội` becomes `duong-pho-ha-noi`.

## Install

Requires Python 3.10 or later. Install from the repository:

```bash
pip install git+https://github.com/example-org/slugkit
```

## Usage

```python
from slugkit import slugify

slugify("Đường phố Hà Nội")                   # 'duong-pho-ha-noi'
slugify("Hello brave new world", max_length=11)  # 'hello-brave'
```

## Development

```bash
pip install -e ".[dev]"
pytest
```

## License

Apache-2.0. See [LICENSE](LICENSE).

# lisa-skills **Reusable AI agent skills for everyday workflows.**
Built for personal use, shared with the community. [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-2ea44f?style=flat-square)](LICENSE) [![Format: Agent Skills](https://img.shields.io/badge/format-Agent%20Skills-6e40c9?style=flat-square)](https://agentskills.io) [![Install with npx skills](https://img.shields.io/badge/install-npx%20skills%20add-cb3837?style=flat-square&logo=npm&logoColor=white)](#quick-start) [![Last commit](https://img.shields.io/github/last-commit/LisaHQ/lisa-skills?style=flat-square&color=0969da)](https://github.com/LisaHQ/lisa-skills/commits/main) [Quick start](#quick-start) · [Skill catalog](#skill-catalog) · [Usage](#usage) · [Create a skill](#create-a-skill) · [Contributing](#contributing)
**lisa-skills** is a curated collection of skills that teach AI agents to handle everyday tasks consistently. Each skill is a small folder of readable Markdown instructions: install it once, and your agent applies it whenever a task calls for it — no copy-pasting prompts. Skills follow the open [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) format, supported by Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, and many other agents. ## Highlights - 🎯 **Focused** — Each skill does one job, with clear inputs, outputs, and success criteria. - 🔍 **Grounded** — Skills work from evidence in your project, not assumptions. - 🧩 **Portable** — No hard-coded names, brands, or paths; skills adapt to any project. - 🪶 **Lightweight** — Plain Markdown you can review before installing, loaded only when a task needs it. ## Skill catalog | Skill | What it does | | --- | --- | | 📝 [**commit-message**](skills/commit-message/SKILL.md) | Writes accurate, concise commit messages from your actual Git or SVN changes. | > [!TIP] > Run `npx skills add LisaHQ/lisa-skills --list` to see the current catalog > from your terminal without installing anything. ## Quick start You need [Node.js](https://nodejs.org) (current LTS recommended) to run the [`skills`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills) CLI through `npx`. No Node.js? See [Manual installation](#manual-installation). **1. Install the skills** ```bash npx skills add LisaHQ/lisa-skills ``` The CLI detects the agents on your machine and guides you through the remaining choices. **2. Ask your agent** Start a new session and describe the task in plain language — for example, *"Write a commit message for my changes."* Your agent loads the matching skill automatically. **3. Stay up to date** ```bash npx skills update ``` ### Common commands | Task | Command | | --- | --- | | Preview skills without installing | `npx skills add LisaHQ/lisa-skills --list` | | Install a specific skill | `npx skills add LisaHQ/lisa-skills --skill commit-message` | | Install for all your projects | `npx skills add LisaHQ/lisa-skills --global` | | Install for specific agents | `npx skills add LisaHQ/lisa-skills --agent claude-code codex` | | List installed skills | `npx skills list` | | Update installed skills | `npx skills update` | | Remove a skill | `npx skills remove commit-message` | > [!NOTE] > By default, skills install into the current project (for example, > `.claude/skills/` for Claude Code), so you can commit them and share them > with your team. Add `--global` to install them in your user directory (for > example, `~/.claude/skills/`) and use them in every project. ### Manual installation Every skill is just a folder, so you can also copy it into your agent's skills directory by hand. For Claude Code: ```bash git clone https://github.com/LisaHQ/lisa-skills.git mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills cp -r lisa-skills/skills/commit-message ~/.claude/skills/ ``` To limit a skill to one project, copy it into that project's `.claude/skills/` folder instead. Other agents read skills from their own folders — see your agent's documentation or the [skills CLI's list of supported agents](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills#supported-agents). ## Usage Skills work in the background, so there are no commands to memorize. - **Just ask.** Describe what you need. Your agent compares the request with each skill's description and loads the right one. - **Call a skill by name.** Many agents also let you invoke a skill directly — in Claude Code, type `/` (e.g., `/commit-message`). - **Fine-tune with options.** Add details in plain language, such as *"only my staged changes"*, or pass arguments like `/commit-message scope=staged`. For example, with the `commit-message` skill: > **You:** Write a commit message for my staged changes. > > **Agent:** Scope: staged (HEAD → index) — 3 files selected. > ```text Support per-job retry limits - feat(retries): Allow each job to override its retry limit. + Treat zero as an explicit request to disable retries. + Preserve the configured default when no override is provided. ``` The skill only drafts the message. It never stages, commits, or pushes without your permission. ## How skills work A skill is a folder containing a `SKILL.md` file: a short YAML header with a `name` and `description`, followed by step-by-step instructions for the agent. 1. **Discover** — At startup, the agent reads only each skill's name and description. 2. **Activate** — When a request matches a description, the agent loads that skill's full instructions. 3. **Execute** — The agent follows the workflow, opening bundled references or scripts only when needed. Because full instructions load on demand, you can keep many skills installed with very little overhead. Learn more at [agentskills.io](https://agentskills.io). ## Repository structure ```text lisa-skills/ ├── skills/ │ └── / │ ├── SKILL.md # Required: metadata and instructions │ ├── references/ # Optional: detailed docs, loaded on demand │ ├── scripts/ # Optional: helper scripts │ └── assets/ # Optional: templates and other resources ├── AGENTS.md # Conventions for AI agents working on this repo ├── CLAUDE.md # Claude Code–specific additions ├── LICENSE └── README.md ``` ## Create a skill 1. Scaffold a new skill from the `skills/` folder: ```bash cd skills npx skills init my-skill ``` 2. Edit `skills/my-skill/SKILL.md`: - **`name`** — Match the folder name, using lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens only. - **`description`** — Say what the skill does *and when to use it*. Agents rely on this text to decide when to load the skill. - **Instructions** — Keep the skill to one purpose, with clear inputs, outputs, and success criteria. 3. From the repository root, confirm that the skill is discovered: ```bash npx skills add . --list ``` 4. Test it with realistic requests, including incomplete, out-of-scope, and failure cases — not just the happy path. 5. Add the skill to the [skill catalog](#skill-catalog) with a one-line description. See [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) for the complete authoring and verification conventions, and the [Agent Skills specification](https://agentskills.io/specification) for the full format. ## Contributing Ideas, bug reports, and improvements are welcome. - **Report a problem or suggest a skill** — [Open an issue](https://github.com/LisaHQ/lisa-skills/issues). - **Propose a change** — Fork the repository, follow [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md), and open a pull request that explains what changed and how you tested it. Please keep personal data, credentials, and confidential material out of skills, examples, and logs. ## License Released under the [MIT License](LICENSE). Copyright © 2026 LisaHQ. ---

# csvdelta

Compare two CSV files by a key column and see which rows were added, removed,
or changed.

[Tiếng Việt](README.vi.md)

## Install

Requires Python 3.10 or later.

```bash
pipx install git+https://github.com/example-org/csvdelta
```

## Usage

```bash
csvdelta --key sku examples/products-v1.csv examples/products-v2.csv
```

```text
removed  A2
added    A3
changed  A1 price
```

Write the report to a file with `--output report.txt`. Use
`--delimiter ";"` for semicolon-separated files and `--format json` or
`--format csv` for machine-readable output. See the
[configuration guide](docs/configuration.md) for every option and the
[exit codes](#exit-codes) for scripting.

## Upgrading to 2.0

- Rename `--out` to `--output` and `--sep` to `--delimiter`. Abbreviated
  flags are no longer accepted.
- Update links to `docs/config.md`; it is now `docs/configuration.md`.

See the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md) for details.

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | The files have the same rows |
| `1` | At least one row was added, removed, or changed |
| `2` | A file could not be read or the key column is missing |
